There is a new shelf above the old one: 60.05 is the lowest close of the breakout leg, and the lows of the last three sessions are 59.95, 60.95 and 61.00, so the entire leg has held above 59.95. 59.75 sits beneath all of it, beneath the 60.05 close, and above the 59.55 close of 07-31 and the 59.40 of 09-03 — it is not itself a visited close and it rests in a genuine gap. An ordinary chop back toward 60 does not trip it; only a close that puts the whole September leg back inside the August base does, which is precisely the event that says the merchant-power staircase is over. At -2.53% from 61.30 it is 3.4 daily ranges on a 0.74% mover, consistent with the 3.0 I default to and with the structural reading I applied here originally, and it moves protection from -3.25% on cost to roughly flat. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. I am also keeping this position rather than trimming it into the shock for a reason worth naming: Austrian hydro is a merchant power producer, and an energy price shock is the environment in which it earns, so unlike AAL this book's commodity leg is on the receiving side. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg to cushion or compound — and on a day when my whole argument is that a crude spike is a terms-of-trade tax on the euro, an asset that collects the higher energy price in euros is the natural hedge against my own thesis.
